description: Labeled classification set for the ODD evidence profile: real messages with the label a correct evaluation must return. Scored by evals/run-classification-eval.ts against the live model, never inside the deterministic suite. The set states ONE predicate, quoted verbatim from profiles/odd-evidence-v4.json (`questions.scope_changed.criteria.present`) in `predicate`, and every note names the clause of that sentence — or, where the case scores `user_only_decision`, the clause of that question's own criterion — that its label rests on. `scope_changed` and `user_only_decision` are judged by the model; `visual_evidence` is not, because the server computes it from whether an attachment was sent, so a note about it states that computation and is not evidence about model behaviour. Only the questions named in a case's `expected` map are scored; every other question the profile returns is printed but not asserted. A case is contestable by its `note`: a note that does not name the clause a model-judged label rests on makes that label wrong. A case that names `imagePath` attaches that file as one inline image, sent as base64 bytes with no path in the request; the runner fails the case if its request carries zero inline images, and prints the byte count. The runner also refuses to run a set that cannot contradict a constant-label model: every scored question needs at least one expected `present` and one expected `absent` case, and `scope_changed` needs at least four expected `present` cases. Labels are assigned per question per case: each case is scored on every question its own text decides, so a case that scores `scope_changed` also scores `user_only_decision` unless the text cannot decide it, and every case states `visual_evidence`, whose label the server computes from the attachment and never asks the model. A question the text genuinely cannot decide is listed in that case's `undecided` array with a one-clause reason and is left out of `expected`.

predicate.question: scope_changed
predicate.statement: The message asks for a repository change: it requests a new file, an edit, a modification of previously produced work, or a new requirement. A message that states a rule the work must follow from now on ("from now on every X must Y") is a new requirement, even when it uses no creation verb. A message that complains or challenges and also carries a directive to change something ("u should create ...", "u should not omit ...") is a request for that change.

cases.text: i want u to create a list for this feature, place it on the root it should contain a list of things like the should help to take desicions, should obey odd workflow, should not allow uncertainability on the responses
cases.note: present on scope_changed. Predicate clause: 'a new file'. 'i want u to create a list ... place it' asks for a file that does not exist yet, and the rest of the message states what it must contain. The label rests on that request for a new file alone: the text does not say 'the root' is the repository root, and nothing in the label depends on reading it that way. A request phrased as content requirements is still a request for a new file, which a reader matching only 'edit' would miss. absent on user_only_decision, criterion: 'it requests reversible work inside the change it describes' — creating one list file is reversible work, and the message requests no destructive action, installation, dependency change, release, deployment or expansion. visual_evidence is `absent`, and that label is not a model judgement: the server computes it from whether an attachment was sent, this case sends none, and it is therefore not evidence about model behaviour.

cases.note: absent on scope_changed. The message reports that the server restarted and instructs a resume bounded by 'without repeating completed work'; it reports and resumes and requests no change, so it meets no predicate clause — in particular not 'a new requirement' and not 'a modification of previously produced work'. A continuation instruction must not be read as new scope. It keeps `absent`. absent on user_only_decision, criterion: 'it requests reversible work inside the change it describes' — resuming without repeating completed work is a reversible continuation, with no destructive action, installation, dependency change, release, deployment or expansion. visual_evidence is `absent`, and that label is not a model judgement: the server computes it from whether an attachment was sent, this case sends none, and it is therefore not evidence about model behaviour.

It requests no code change at all, which is why the scope label below is the contestable one. present on scope_changed: the predicate's absent clause lists what a non-request does — asks only for information, an explanation, a recommendation or a review, reports on and discusses existing work, or suggests something only for the future — and this message does none of those; it requests work to be performed. cases.text: u added testing that the system one correctly land on the scope changed result is supposend u should create scenarios where is should choose that? u should not omit those tests
cases.note: present on scope_changed. Predicate clause: 'a modification of previously produced work'. Borderline, and recorded as such: the message is phrased as a complaint ('u added testing that ... is supposend'), but it carries two directives — 'u should create scenarios where is should choose that' and 'u should not omit those tests' — which require additional test cases to be added to the tests already produced. Reading only the complaint tone would label it absent; the directives are what the label rests on. absent on user_only_decision, criterion: 'it requests reversible work inside the change it describes' — additional test scenarios are reversible work inside the change the message itself requests, and the challenge tone adds no destructive action, installation, dependency change, release, deployment or expansion. visual_evidence is `absent`, and that label is not a model judgement: the server computes it from whether an attachment was sent, this case sends none, and it is therefore not evidence about model behaviour.
